name: Sunda leopard cat
description:
3D scan of the skull of a Sunda leopard cat (*Prionailurus javanensis*).

The Sunda leopard cat is a small wild cat species native to the Sundaland islands of Java, Bali, Borneo, Sumatra and the Philippines that is considered distinct from the leopard cat occurring in mainland South and Southeast Asia. It has a head-body lengths of 39 to 66 cm and tail about 40–50% of that length. It lives in lowland tropical evergreen forest, but it has also adapted to human-modified landscapes with suitable vegetation cover where it feeds mainly on rodents, lizards, snakes, frogs and beetles.

Specimen: Sunda leopard cat, *Prionailurus javanensis* (Desmarest, 1816)

 Inventory number: C 751
 
Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

Scanned and edited by Simone Farina

name: 3D ROBOT BUTTERFLY
description:
3D ROBOT BUTTERFLY
The object represents a robot inspired by a monarch butterfly. The wings are designed with intricate details that mimic the structure and colours of the actual wings of this species, with orange, black and white patterns reminiscent of its organic texture but with a mechanical touch.

The robot's body appears to be composed of gears, bolts and nut-like elements, giving it a steampunk style. The legs have joints made of rods and small metal cylinders, which makes it possible to imagine that they could move in a precise manner. The eyes stand out as circular lenses, giving the appearance of advanced scopes or sensors.

Overall, the combination of the mechanical and the natural results in a fascinating design that balances technology and art.

name: Channel catfish
description:
Найпопулярніший сом у Північній Америці – Це найбільш поширений вид сома в США, популярний серед рибалок і розводиться в аквакультурі для харчових потреб.
Чутливі вусики – Його вусики навколо рота виконують роль сенсорних органів, допомагаючи знаходити їжу навіть у каламутній воді. Він відчуває запахи набагато краще за людей!
Всеїдний харчовий режим – Channel Catfish їсть майже все: рибу, комах, ракоподібних, рослинний матеріал і навіть мертву органіку, що робить його природним "прибиральником" водойм.
Рекордні розміри – Зазвичай ця риба важить 2–5 кг, але найбільший зафіксований екземпляр важив 26,3 кг і був спійманий у Південній Кароліні.
Незвичайний спосіб розмноження – Самці викопують гніздо в укритті (під корінням або в норах), де самка відкладає ікру. Після цього самець охороняє яйця та молодь, доки вони не зміцніють.

name: Thylacinus cynocephalus - MNCN-M2613
description:
**Description**: This 3D model represents the thylacine or Tasmanian tiger, a legendary carnivorous marsupial extinct since 1936 and famous for its astonishing evoulutionary convergence with canids. This specimen from the MNCN preserves the memory of a unique species whose branch on the tree of life was tragically cut short in the last century.

**Specimen**: *Thylacinus cynocephalus*  (Harris, 1808)

**Inventory number**: MNCN-M2613

**Collection**: Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales, Mamíferos. Curator: Ángel Garvía (colecciondemamiferos@mncn.csic.es)

**More about**:

Find more about the MNCN [here](http:mncn.csic.es/en).

Find more about the thylacine [here](http:mncn.csic.es/es/comunicacion/blog/la-extincion-de-un-mamifero-legendario).

Scanned with an Artec Eva in 2025 by Carlos A. Palancar.

name: Elephant Wreck - Dahab, Egypt
description:
**Elephant Wreck**

Location: Lighthouse Dive Site,  28° 29' 56 ''N ,34° 31' 11 ''E

Depth: ~20-28m

The Elephant was built in 2014 in Dahab City, Sinai, and it actually is not the only sculpture there. According to the Facebook page “Best hang out places in Egypt”, there is another sculpture of a pharaoh symbol, with three more sculptures planned.

This is an ecological initiative that has been followed by many great countries, such as America and Thailand. These sculptures are made of metal skeletons to help the coral reefs grow. If you love diving or scuba diving, you will find this quite enjoyable, as you can go take pictures with these sculptures.

Squirrels primarily feed on nuts, fruits, and seeds, though they sometimes eat insects. They have a habit of storing food for winter, burying acorns and walnuts in the ground. name: Southeastern four-eyed opossum
description:
3D scan of the skull of a southeastern four-eyed opossum (*Philander frenatus*).

The southeastern four-eyed opossum is a marsupial which lives in South America, in the Atlantic forest ecoregions, in Brazil, Paraguay and Argentina. It is a large dark gray opossum. Dorsal fur is dark gray, and the fur on the sides is also gray, but lighter than the dorsal fur. The ventral fur is white or cream-colored. The hairs on the throat have gray bases, but are divided in two by a cream-colored vertical stripe going along the midline of the throat. It feeds mainly on arthropods and small vertebrates, suplementing its diet with fruits. 

Specimen: Southeastern four-eyed opossum, *Philander frenatus*  (Olfers, 1818)

Inventory number: C 1260

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

Scanned and edited by Marco Merella and Enrique Sierra

name: Tell El-Ghaba, Figurine 321-98
description:
The three-dimensional Nile silt clay model designated F0321, originating from Tell El-Ghaba, represents a carefully crafted example of early material culture from the site. This zoomorphic figurine represents a sheep and was recovered from the Level II of  Building L. The piece is executed in fine, well-levigated clay, moulded by hand into a compact volumetric form. Its surfaces exhibit traces of smoothing, suggesting intentional finishing, although minor irregularities remain visible, consistent with artisanal rather than mass-produced manufacture.

Bibliography:
Lupo, S. (ed.) 2015. Tell el-Ghaba III. A Third Intermediate-Early Saite Period site in the Egyptian eastern Delta. Excavations 1995-1999 and 2010 in areas I, II, VI and VIII. BAR International Series 2756, p. 359, fig. 11. Oxford: Archaeopress.

name: Brown four-eyed opossum
description:
3D scan of the mandible of a brown four-eyed opossum (*Metachirus nudicaudatus*).

The brown four-eyed opossum is a pouchless marsupial of the family Didelphidae which lives in forested habitats of Central and South America at elevations from sea level to 1,500 m. It is a nocturnal animal, solitary, terrestrial with an omnivorous diet, feeding on fruits, small vertebrates and invertebrates. 


Specimen: Brown four-eyed opossum, *Metachirus nudicaudatus* (E'. Geoffroy, 1803)

Inventory number: C 978

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

Scanned and edited by Marco Merella and Enrique Sierra

name: Cat vertebral column
description: This model shows the vertebral column, or backbone, of a cat running from behind the head to the pelvis, near the hindlimbs. Notice how the vertebrae are arranged in groups? These are called regions, and that is a distinctive feature of mammals! Here we can see the Neck (red), thoracic or rib-bearing (yellow), and lumbar or ribless (blue) vertebrae, with some transitional vertebrae in between.

name: Tell El-Ghaba, Figurine SCA-973
description:
The three-dimensional Nile silt clay model designated F0001/ SCA973, from Tell El-Ghaba, represents a horse with a rider. The piece is executed in fine, well-levigated clay, moulded by hand into a compact volumetric form. Legs and part of the body of a rider on the back of the horse are present. Its surfaces exhibit traces of smoothing, suggesting intentional finishing, although minor irregularities remain visible, consistent with artisanal rather than mass-produced manufacture.

Bibliography:
Fuscaldo, P. (ed.) 2005. Tell el-Ghaba I. A Saite Settlement in North Sinai, Egypt (Argentine Archaeological Mission 1995-2004). Vol I. The Catalogue (Colección Estudios 5), p. 143, fig. 40:38. Buenos Aires: CONICET.
Lupo, S. (ed.) 2015. Tell el-Ghaba III. A Third Intermediate-Early Saite Period site in the Egyptian eastern Delta. Excavations 1995-1999 and 2010 in areas I, II, VI and VIII. BAR International Series 2756, p. 359, fig. 11. Oxford: Archaeopress.

description:
Ferocious Venusaur - The Mighty Seed Pokémon!
Unleash the power of the original grass titan! This stunning miniature presents a more realistic and fierce interpretation of Venusaur, the final evolution of Bulbasaur, ready to dominate your display shelf or gaming table.

Its intense, glowing orange eyes convey a primal strength and a hint of aggression, reimagining this beloved Pokémon with a formidable edge.

description: The balloon worm (Poeobius meseres) is a unique, gelatinous marine worm found in the midwater (mesopelagic and bathypelagic zones) of the ocean, typically at depths of 300-2,500 meters (980-8,200 feet). The balloon worm (Poeobius meseres) is a specialized marine worm that, despite its gelatinous, unsegmented appearance, belongs to the phylum of segmented worms (Annelida). It is a holopelagic species, meaning it spends its entire life cycle floating in the midwater column (mesopelagic and bathypelagic zones) rather than living on the seafloor.

name: Little owl
description:
3D scan of a skeleton of little owl (*Athene noctua*). 

The little owl is a bird member of the family Strigidae that inhabits much of the temperate and warmer parts of Europe, the Palearctic east to Korea, and North Africa. t is a small (approx. 22 cm long), cryptically coloured, mainly nocturnal species and is found in a range of habitats including farmland, woodland fringes, steppes and semi-deserts. It feeds on insects, earthworms, other invertebrates and small vertebrates.


Specimen: little owl, *Athene noctua* (Scopoli, 1769)

Inventory number: AV 7154

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

Scanned and edited by Simone Farina 

Scanner: Artec spider

name: Spectacled hare-wallaby tibia
description:
Left tibia of a spectacled hare-wallaby (*Lagorchestes conspicillatus*).

3D model produced by a structured light surface scan of specimen UQ-278 from the collection of the University of Queensland Archaeology Laboratories. Specimen scanned using a Solutionix C500. Digitisation funded by Ozboneviz, an ARC Centre of Excellence for Australian Biodiversity and Heritage project. Further editing in Blender.

Original data available on MorphoSource [DOI: 10.17602/M2/M447322](https://doi.org/10.17602/M2/M447322)

name: Sculpture "Still Water" in Almaty, 2016
description:
Скульптура «Still Water» («Спокойная вода») в Алматы — это впечатляющее произведение британского скульптора Ника Фиддиана-Грина (Nic Fiddian-Green), известного своими монументальными изображениями лошадей. Она представляет собой голову лошади, словно опущенную к воде, и установлена в парковой зоне Esentai Park, недалеко от проспекта Аль-Фараби.

Скульптура выполнена из бронзы и достигает около 3 метров в высоту. Голова лошади балансирует на кончике носа, создавая ощущение легкости и гармонии с окружающей природой. По замыслу автора, лошадь пришла на водопой, и ее голова как бы выглядывает из облаков или зелени, в зависимости от ракурса. Эта работа является частью серии скульптур «Still Water», установленных в разных городах мира, включая Лондон и Сингапур.

Охрана Есентая запрещала снимать этот памятник.

The siamang is an endangered arboreal, black-furred gibbon native to the forests of Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand. The largest of the gibbons, the siamang can be twice the size of other gibbons, reaching 1 m in height, and weighing up to 14 kg. It inhabits the forest remnants of Sumatra Island and the Malay Peninsula, and is widely distributed from lowland forest to mountain forest—even rainforest—and can be found at altitudes up to 3800 m. The siamang eats mainly various parts of plants.

description: A medieval stone statue of a hawk, crafted with a blend of strength and elegance befitting the era. The hawk stands proudly on a rugged stone pedestal, its stance vigilant and majestic. Its eyes are deeply carved, set in a piercing gaze that seems to survey its surroundings with an air of dominance. The beak is sharply defined, slightly hooked, and chiseled to emphasize its fierce predatory nature. Its wings are partially unfurled, with each feather carefully etched in layers, capturing both the power and grace of the bird in flight. The body is muscular and robust, suggesting the hawk's readiness to swoop down at any moment. Its talons are clenched tightly around the base, gripping with an intensity that conveys strength and control. The statue's surface is weathered and aged, with patches of moss and erosion marking the passage of time, adding to its ancient and enduring character.

name: Crimson Fanglurker - spider
description:
**The Crimson Fanglurker**  
*Scientific Name: Araneus sanguimandibula*

First documented in the mist-laden caves of the Carpathian Basin in 1837, the Crimson Fanglurker is a rare arachnid species known for its oversized chelicerae and mottled crimson abdomen. Measuring nearly 30 cm across, this solitary predator uses its twelve clustered eyes to detect prey in near-total darkness. Its fangs, coated in hemotoxic venom, earned it the nickname “Bloodjaw” among local folklore.

Despite its terrifying appearance, the Fanglurker is a slow-moving ambush hunter, relying on camouflage and vibration-sensitive hairs to detect movement. Its coloration shifts subtly with age, from earthy browns to deep reds, believed to signal maturity and mating readiness. Though sightings are rare, its legend persists in rural Romanian ghost stories, where it’s said to guard ancient burial sites and feed only under a blood moon.

name: Pleistocene Canis Proximal Phalanx UW57662
description: This 3D model represents UW-57662, a proximal phalanx (the first bone of a toe) from the genus Canis, discovered in 2022 at Natural Trap Cave (on Bureau of Land Managment land, and curated at the University of Wyoming).  The bone dates to the Pleistocene and may belong to either a wolf or a coyote—distinguishing between the two is challenging because research from Natural Trap Cave has shown that Ice Age coyotes were significantly larger than their modern counterparts, creating strong overlap with wolves. Natural Trap Cave itself is an 85-foot limestone pit near the Bighorn Mountains that acted as a natural animal trap for tens of thousands of years, preserving an exceptional record of Ice Age fauna. This specimen is part of that rich archive of Wyoming’s Pleistocene predators.

name: Red-tailed hawk
description:
Зовнішній вигляд: Червонохвостий яструб має широкі крила і короткий, але помітний червоно-коричневий хвіст, який стає яскравішим у дорослих особин. Його забарвлення варіюється, але зазвичай верхня частина тіла коричнева, а нижня — світла з темними смугами. Розмах крил сягає 1,1–1,4 м.
Ареал: Цей вид поширений по всій Північній Америці — від Аляски та Канади до Центральної Америки й Карибських островів. Він адаптується до різних середовищ: лісів, прерій, пустель і навіть міських зон.
Полювання: Червонохвостий яструб — вправний хижак. Він полює на дрібних ссавців (мишей, кроликів), птахів, рептилій і навіть комах, чатуючи з висоти або ширяючи в небі. Його гострий зір дозволяє помічати здобич з великої відстані, а пронизливий крик часто асоціюється з образом яструба в поп-культурі.
Гніздування: Ці яструби будують великі гнізда з гілок у верхівках високих дерев або на скелях, які можуть використовувати кілька років поспіль.

name: ピグミーシロナガスクジラ（東海大学海洋科学博物館所蔵）
description:
ピグミーシロナガスクジラ（ *Balaenoptera musculus brevicauda* ）の交連骨格標本3Dモデルデータ 東海大学海洋科学博物館所蔵

本3Dモデルデータは2025年まで東海大学海洋科学博物館にて展示・保管されていたピグミーシロナガスクジラの骨格標本を撮影、フォトグラメトリーにより再構築したものです。当該標本は1966年12月25日にマダガスカル島と南極大陸の間の海域で採集された雄の個体であり、全長約18.6ｍ、体重約43.0トン、骨重量は約3.5トンとなります。また当該標本は2026年現在、本邦唯一の全身骨格標本となります。

2026年1月現在、当該標本は解体され、ふじのくに地球環境史ミュージアム（静岡県）に保管されています。本データは一般社団法人路上博物館により2025年に撮影されました。

description:
Spinnerbait fishing lures have metal blades that spin like a propeller when the lure is in motion, creating varying degrees of flash and vibration in the water. Spinnerbaits are used principally for catching predatory fish such as perch, pike and bass, and are particularly helpful in attracting fish as you begin your day out on the lake.

A spinnerbait or spinner is any one of a family of hybrid fishing lures that combines the designs of a swimbait with one or more spoon lure blades. Spinnerbaits get the name from the action of the metallic blades, which passively revolve around the attachment point like a spinning propeller when the lure is in motion, creating varying degrees of vibration and flashing that mimic small fish or other preys of interest to large predatory fishes.

description:
3D scan of the skull of a sun bear (*Helarctos malayanus*).

The sun bear is a bear species found in the tropical forests of Southeast Asia. It is the smallest bear species, standing nearly 70 cm at the shoulder and weighing 25–65 kg. It is the most arboreal of all bears, it is an excellent climber and sunbathes or sleeps in trees 2 to 7 m above the ground. It has an omnivorous diet and it feeds on ants, bees, beetles, honey, termites, and plant material such as seeds and several kinds of fruits.

Description
The adult spider is black. 

Females have a characteristic red hourglass-shaped spot on the underside of the abdomen and several red spots near the spider webs and on the back. The body length of the female is 8–10 mm. 

Males differ from females in their small size (3–4 mm in length) and elongated abdomen (in females it is round). The legs of males are painted in orange and black stripes, and there are red and white marks on the sides of the abdomen. 

Young spiderlings are white or yellowish-white and darken with each subsequent molt. 

Habitat
Black widows prefer warm regions: Central Asia, Southern Europe, North Africa. 

Habitat: steppes and deserts, ravine slopes, rodent burrows, soil cracks, under rocks and in plant roots. 

Danger to humans
The black widow is not aggressive towards humans and bites them only for self-defense in a desperate situation (for example, if the spider is crushed by hand).

name: Greater glider
description:
3D scan of the mandible of the southern greater glider (*Petauroides volans*).

The southern greater glider is a large gliding marsupial native to the forests of southeastern Australia.  It is the one of the world’s largest gliding mammals (its body spans 35-46 cm), growing to the size of a house cat. It lives in a variety of eucalipt forest, from low, open forests on the coast to low woodlands in eastern and south-eastern Australia. It feeds almost entirely on young leaves, buds and flowers of trees of the myrtle family.


Specimen: Southern greater glider, *Petauroides volans* (Kerr, 1792)

Inventory number: C 990

name: Flamingo
description:
3D scan of a skull of flamingo (*Phoenicopterus* sp.). 


*Phoenicopterus* is a genus of birds in the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae. The genus contains three extant species: Greater flamingo (*Phoenicopterus roseus*) widespread in Africa and southwest, south-central Eurasia, American flamingo (*Phoenicopterus ruber*) which inhabits northern Galápagos Islands and the Caribbean, and Chilean flamingo (*Phoenicopterus chilensis*)  which inhabits central Peru to Tierra del Fuego east to south Brazil, Uruguay and central Argentina. All flamingos are filter feeders: they eat algae, small seeds, tiny crustaceans (like brine shrimp), fly larvae, and other plants and animals that live in shallow waters.


Specimen: Flamingo, *Phoenicopterus* sp.

Arapaima gigas

The paiche, pirarucu, or arapaima is one of the largest freshwater fish in the world, growing to over 3 meters in length and weighing up to 250 kg.

In Brazil, it is known as “pirarucu,” a name that comes from the Tupi language and means “red fish.”

This fish inhabits the rivers of the Amazon rainforest basin and is primarily carnivorous, feeding on smaller fish, although it may also consume plant matter and crustaceans.

They are perfectly adapted to habitats with low oxygen concentrations, especially during the dry season. Its main threat is overfishing.

name: Waorani Robber Frog
description:
Quad mesh, 3072 vertices, Basecolor, roughness, normal map, 30 fps animation, 60 frames, Made in Blender and Substance Painter.


Pristimantis waoranii

It is endemic to Ecuador, specifically to the province of Orellana, and inhabits terra firme forest, flooded forest, seasonally flooded areas, and palm swamps.

It is named in honor of the Waorani tribe, an Indigenous ethnic group that has inhabited the region for many years.

Its habitat is being fragmented by oil extraction activities, agriculture, deforestation, the introduction of invasive species, and human settlements.

It is listed on the Ecuadorian Amphibian Red List as Near Threatened under Criterion D2.

name: カバトゲウミギク / Spondylus butleri
description:
殻は類円形で大型になり、右殻で岩礁などに固着して生活する。橙色、赤紫色などの個体がある。左右の殻の色違いは非常に珍しい。紀伊半島以南、インド・西太平洋に分布し、水深5～20ｍの岩礁に生息。

The shell is subcircular and grows to a large size; the right valve attaches to rocky reefs and other substrates. Some individuals are orange or reddish-purple in color. It is extremely rare for the left and right valves to differ in color. This species is found south of the Kii Peninsula, as well as in the Indian and Western Pacific Oceans, inhabiting rocky reefs at depths of 5 to 20 meters.

name: Suchomimus
description:
Suchomimus was a remarkable spinosaurid dinosaur that roamed the Early Cretaceous period, approximately 125 million years ago. Discovered in what is now Niger, Africa, this massive theropod measured around 36 feet (11 meters) in length and weighed between 3 and 5 tons. Unlike other typical large theropods, Suchomimus had a long, narrow skull filled with conical, crocodile-like teeth, perfectly adapted for catching fish. Its snout was elongated with a distinctive kink near the tip, a feature seen in modern-day gharials, which helped it grip slippery prey such as fish and other aquatic creatures.

One of its most striking features was the large sail-like ridge along its back, formed by elongated neural spines. While not as pronounced as Spinosaurus, this structure may have played a role in thermoregulation, display, or muscle attachment for a powerful body structure.

name: Acrocanthosaurus  NCSM 14345 Pes Ungual
description:
Photogrammetry scan of the toe claw of [Acrocanthosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acrocanthosaurus) NCSM 14345

Acrocanthosaurus is a genus of carcharodontosaurid dinosaurs that existed in what is now North America during the Aptian and early Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous, from 113 to 110 million years ago. Like most dinosaur genera, Acrocanthosaurus contains only a single species, A. atokensis. It had a continent-wide range, with fossil remains known from the U.S. states of Oklahoma, Texas, and Wyoming in the west and Maryland in the east. However, most of these remains are assigned to the species based on the assumption that Acrocanthosaurus is the only large carcharodontosaurid from North America during this time, and the possibility exists that some referred specimens could represent distinct taxa. 

The claw is 118MM in length

From Wikipedia: 

Pholas dactylus, or common piddock, is a bioluminescent clam-like species of marine mollusc in the family Pholadidae.

The piddock bores into the substrate for shelter, and lives in a tubular burrow formed by grinding the material away with hard parts of the shell by rotating on the longitudinal axis. It has been known to bore into the hard metamorphic rock gneiss, though it more often lives in softer rock. It is a filter feeder, using its siphons to reach the water outside the burrow.

name: Common warthog
description:
3D scan of the mandible of a Common warthog (*Phacochoerus africanus*). 

The common warthog is a wild member of the pig family found in grassland, savannah, and woodland in sub-Saharan Africa. It is identifiable by the two pairs of tusks protruding from the mouth and curving upwards. The lower pair, which is far shorter than the upper pair, becomes razor-sharp by rubbing against the upper pair every time the mouth is opened and closed. It has an head and body length of 0.9-1.5 m and a weight of 45-150 kg  (males are bigger than females). It has an omnivorous diet, composed of grasses, roots, berries and other fruits, bark, fungi, insects, eggs and carrion.

name: Ammonite fossil
description:
Fosil Amonites.

El fósil amonites proviene de un molusco cefalópodo, los ammonoideos. Estas criaturas habitaron nuestro planeta hace 400 millones de años.
Los ammonites son animales marinos que prosperaron en las Eras Paleozoicas y Mesozoicas, parientes extintos de los calamares, pulpos, sepias y nautilos que conocemos en nuestros días.

Podían nadar gracias a la construcción única de su caparazón, que se dividía en una serie de cámaras de aire. El aire proporcionaba flotabilidad al animal, y al igual que los cefalópodos modernos las amonitas se movían por el los océanos y mares usando propulsión a chorro.

Como las amonitas vivían exclusivamente en ambientes marinos, su presencia nos indica indica la ubicación de los mares prehistóricos como el Mar de Tetis.

name: Cráneo Delfín 🐬
description:
El delfín (tursiops truncatus) es un mamífero marino perteneciente a la familia Delphinidae, ampliamente conocido por su inteligencia, comportamiento social y agilidad en el agua. Vive en grupos llamados manadas y se comunica mediante sonidos complejos y ecolocalización. Su cuerpo es aerodinámico, con un hocico alargado y una aleta dorsal que lo caracteriza. Se alimenta principalmente de peces y calamares, y utiliza estrategias cooperativas para cazar. Los delfines desempeñan un papel clave en los ecosistemas marinos, y aunque muchas especies están protegidas, enfrentan amenazas como la contaminación, la pesca incidental y la degradación de su hábitat.

description:
**Description**: *Helix amori* (Hidalgo, 1867) (Syntype). Collected in Tena, Ecuador by Francisco de Paula Martínez y Sáez during the Scientific Commission of the Pacific (1862–1866): a major 19th-century Spanish expedition. Aided by a naval squadron, naturalists traveled across South America and California, collecting over 80,000 natural specimens. The mission culminated in an overland trek across the Andes and Amazon. Notably, they collected 40,000 mollusks, yielding 35 newly described species now preserved at the MNCN.

**Specimen**: *Helix amori* (Hidalgo, 1867)

**Inventory number**: MNCN-15.05/3169

**Collection**: Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales, Malacología. Curators: Lola Bragado (lolab@mncn.csic.es) and Javier de Andrés Cobeta (javiermol@mncn.csic.es)

name: Dromedary
description:
3D scan of the skeleton of a dromedary (*Camelus dromedarius*). 

The dromedary is a large camel with one hump on its back. It is the tallest of the three species of camel with adult males stand 1.8–2.4 m. It feeds on foliage and desert vegetation. The dromedary has not occurred naturally in the wild for nearly 2,000 years. It was probably first domesticated in the Arabian Peninsula about 4,000 years ago. In the wild, the dromedary inhabited arid regions, including the Sahara Desert. The domesticated dromedary is generally found in the semi-arid to arid regions of the Old World, mainly in Africa and the Arabian Peninsula, and a significant feral population occurs in Australia.

name: Elephant Bird
description:
Once the largest bird to ever walk the Earth, the Elephant Bird (Aepyornis maximus) was a flightless giant native to the island of Madagascar. Standing over 3 meters (10 feet) tall and weighing up to 700 kilograms (1,500 pounds), this towering avian relic dominated its ecosystem with sheer size.

This 3D model captures the elephant bird in lifelike detail, featuring:
	•	A massive, powerful frame built for slow but steady movement
	•	Dense, coarse feathering similar to that of modern-day ostriches or emus
	•	A thick, slightly hooked beak adapted for a herbivorous diet
	•	Large, talon-like feet that gripped the forest floor

Despite its intimidating bulk, the elephant bird was a gentle giant, browsing on fruits and foliage. Sadly, it went extinct around the 17th century, likely due to habitat loss and human activity.

Today, it stands as a symbol of prehistoric mystery — a feathered colossus from a lost age.

name: PYROCERATOPS
description:
**PYROCERATOPS** is a high-detail organic creature inspired by ceratopsian dinosaurs and reimagined with a dark, volcanic fantasy aesthetic. The model features a rugged, lava-cracked skin surface with deep scale definition, giving it a haunted jungle and molten stone appearance. The primary body uses a rich red color palette with natural variation, while the horns and spikes are textured in a realistic greyish-white bone material to create strong visual contrast.

The creature is fully modeled from scratch in Autodesk Maya, with carefully planned topology and a clean UV layout. Custom 4K PBR textures were created using the exact UV unwrap, including Base Color, Normal, Bump, and Roughness maps, ensuring a highly realistic surface response under lighting. This asset is suitable for fantasy scenes, cinematic renders, creature showcases, and real-time environments.

name: Desmodus Requiem "Vampire" - Curse of the West
description:
After a mining collapse sealed 19 workers inside a flooded cavern, they were trapped with a colony of massive blood-drinking bats that had evolved feeding on blind cavefish. The bats wouldn't feed on humans—too similar. But starvation changed things. The next generation emerged tall, thin, humanoid. Fish-coded wings. Cold-blooded. Parasitic. They rise once a year for a month to drink from living hosts. They don’t kill—their saliva paralyzes. Victims who die usually bite it after, cold and disoriented. The worst part isn't being bitten. Its seeing 3 of them next year with your features cloned afterwards.

I recently had my health re-evaluated and was told I likely have about two years left—if I’m very lucky. The cause is complications from past abdominal surgeries that, unfortunately, weren’t taken seriously enough by those around me at the time.
Because of this, I’ve decided to share more of my unfinished, unrefined, and conceptual work. 
I’d truly love to hear your thoughts on these creations and concepts.

description:
This is a 3D digital model of a partial pig mandible (Sus scrofa domesticus), excavated in Jarrow. The model represents one lateral side of the lower jaw, preserving key anatomical features including part of the mandibular body and ascending ramus, with the condyle and coronoid process partially or fully visible depending on preservation.

Dentition and/or alveolar structures are present along the preserved section, with surface detail capturing bone texture, wear, and minor post-depositional alterations.

The model was produced using digital recording techniques (e.g., photogrammetry), allowing for accurate visualisation, measurement, and analysis for research and teaching purposes.

name: African Bush Elephant
description:
African elephants are members of the genus Loxodonta comprising two living elephant species, the African bush elephant (L. africana) and the smaller African forest elephant (L. cyclotis). Both are social herbivores with grey skin. However, they differ in the size and colour of their tusks as well as the shape and size of their ears and skulls.

Both species are at a pertinent risk of extinction according to the IUCN Red List; as of 2021, the bush elephant is considered endangered while the forest elephant is considered critically endangered. They are threatened by habitat loss and fragmentation, along with poaching for the illegal ivory trade in several range countries.

Loxodonta is one of two extant genera in the family Elephantidae. The name refers to the lozenge-shaped enamel of their molar teeth. Fossil remains of Loxodonta species have been found in Africa, spanning from the Late Miocene (from around 7–6 million years ago) onwards.

Known as the "hunting hyena" due to its gracile skeleton and sectorial dentition, this species lived in the Iberian Peninsula throughout the Pliocene epoch.

**Inventory number**: MNCNPV-67100 

**Collection**: Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales, Paleontología de Vertebrados. Curator: Susana Fraile (susana.fraile@mncn.csic.es)

name: hydronephrosis pig
description:
Hydronephrosis of a pig 

size of specimen: 131.8 x 96.2 x 27.2mm

3D scanning performed with the structured light scanner Artec Space Spider

Etiology: Congenital malformations (e.g., ureteral ectopia), urolithiasis, inflammation, fibrosis, or neoplasia causing ureteral obstruction.

Pathogenesis: Obstructed urine flow increases pelvic pressure, leading to progressive dilation, cortical thinning, and renal parenchymal atrophy.

Epidemiology: Occurs sporadically; prevalence in slaughter pigs ~0.7 %. May 
affect individuals or small groups within a herd.

Clinical Signs: Often asymptomatic if unilateral. In bilateral or advanced cases: poor growth, abdominal distension, discomfort.

Diagnosis: Gross pathology shows pelvic dilation, thin cortex. Confirmed via ultrasonography or MRI; histology shows atrophic parenchyma and hydroureter.

name: Эукариотическая клетка
description: Эукариотическая клетка человека представляет собой сложную, высокоорганизованную биологическую систему, являющуюся элементарной структурно-функциональной единицей всех тканей и органов человеческого организма. В отличие от прокариотических клеток (бактерий и архей), эукариотическая клетка человека обладает оформленным клеточным ядром, отделённым от цитоплазмы двойной ядерной мембраной с порами, что позволяет пространственно разделить процессы репликации, транскрипции и трансляции генетической информации. Размеры соматических клеток человека варьируют от 10 до 100 мкм в диаметре, а форма может быть самой разнообразной — округлой (лейкоциты), плоской (эпителиоциты), веретеновидной (фибробласты, гладкомышечные клетки), отростчатой (нейроны), двояковогнутой (эритроциты) — и строго коррелирует с выполняемой функцией.

name: Tammar wallaby
description:
3D scan of the skull of a tammar wallaby (*Notamacropus eugenii*). 

The tammar wallaby is a small wallaby native to South and Western Australia. It features a proportionally small head with large ears, and an elongated tail, with a thick base. It has dark greyish upperparts with a paler underside and rufous-coloured sides and limbs. It has a marked sexual dimorphism: males has an head and body length from 59 to 68 cm weighting 9.1 kg while females are considerably smaller (head and body length from 52 to 63 cm weighting 6.9 kg). The tail has a length of 34 to 45 cm for males and 33 to 44 cm for females. It has an herbivorous diet, feeding on grasses and shrubs.



Specimen: Tammar wallaby, *Notamacropus eugenii* (Desmarest, 1817) 

Inventory number: C 136

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

Scanned and edited by Marco Merella and Enrique Sierra

Scanner: Artec Spider

name: Nest - Strong-billed honeyeater
description:
**Strong-billed honeyeater, *Melithreptus validirostris***


Strong-billed honeyeater nests are cup-shaped and made of fibrous bark and grass, bound with spider web and lined with fur or the soft fibre from tree ferns. The nests are placed from two to twenty metres above ground in the outer foliage of a tree.

Strong-billed honeyeaters usually lay three salmon-pink eggs with reddish-brown spots. 
IMAGE: Clutch of three strong-billed honeyeater eggs, length 22.0 mm. QVM:2006:2:1607
